## 2. Business Process Flowchart

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Customer Places Order] --> B{Order Channel?}
  
    B -->|Online| C[Web Storefront]
    B -->|In-Store| D[POS System]
  
    C --> E[Create Order Record]
    D --> E
  
    E --> F[Process Payment]
    F --> G{Payment Successful?}
  
    G -->|Yes| H[Update Inventory]
    G -->|No| I[Reject Order → Notify Customer]
  
    H --> J{Order Contains Physical Items?}
    J -->|Yes| K[Create Shipping Record]
    J -->|No| L[Digital Delivery]
  
    K --> M[Assign Carrier & Tracking]
    M --> N[Ship to Customer]
    N --> O[Delivery Confirmed]
  
    O --> P[Customer Receives Order]
    P --> Q{Customer Satisfied?}
  
    Q -->|Yes| R[Leave Positive Review]
    Q -->|No| S[Initiate Return/Exchange]
  
    R --> T[Update Review Table]
    S --> U[Process Return]
  
    L --> P
  
    subgraph "Inventory Management"
        V[Monitor Stock Levels] --> W{Quantity ≤ Reorder Point?}
        W -->|Yes| X[Trigger Reorder]
        W -->|No| Y[No Action]
        X --> Z[Restock from Publisher]
        Z --> V
    end
  
    H --> V
```

## 3. Sequence Diagram — Order Lifecycle

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor Customer
    participant Web as Web Storefront / POS
    participant DB as Bookstore Database
    participant Pay as Payment Gateway
    participant Ship as Shipping Carrier

    Customer->>Web: Browse catalog / Add to cart
    Web->>DB: Query books (JOIN books, categories, inventory)
    DB-->>Web: Return book details + stock

    Customer->>Web: Checkout
    Web->>DB: INSERT order (orders table)
    Web->>DB: INSERT order_items (order_items table)
    Web->>DB: UPDATE inventory (decrement quantity)
  
    Web->>Pay: Process payment
    Pay-->>Web: Payment confirmation
    Web->>DB: INSERT payment record (payments table)
  
    alt Online Order
        Web->>Ship: Create shipment
        Ship-->>Web: Tracking number
        Web->>DB: INSERT shipping record (shipping table)
    end
  
    DB-->>Web: Order confirmed
    Web-->>Customer: Order confirmation email

    Note over DB: Periodic: Analytics queries run by analyst
    Note over DB: reviews table updated by customer post-delivery
```

## 5. Key Design Observations

| Aspect                            | Observation                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Channel inference**       | `orders.store_id` is the de facto channel indicator: NULL = online, non-NULL = physical store. A dedicated `channel` column would improve clarity. |
| **Many-to-many**            | `book_authors` links books to authors with ordering (`author_order`), supporting co-authored works.                                                |
| **Hierarchical categories** | `categories.parent_category_id` self-references for genre/sub-genre hierarchy (e.g., "Fiction" → "Literary Fiction").                               |
| **No direct promo linkage** | `promotions` are not linked to `orders` via FK. Analyst must infer promotional impact through discount patterns or temporal analysis.              |
| **Employee-store link**     | `employees.store_id` links staff to locations; `stores.manager_id` references an employee as store manager.                                        |
| **Date format risk**        | Multiple date formats across the dataset require careful parsing before time-series analysis.                                                          |
